heading_en: Risk Weights of Qualifying Short-Term STC Securitization Exposures
summary_ja: 適格短期STC証券化エクスポージャーのリスク・ウェイトに前条第一項及び第二項を準用し、その定義と、トランザクションの適格要件及びABCP証券化目的導管体の適格要件を定める。
summary_en: Applies the preceding Article's treatment to qualifying short-term STC securitization exposures (ABCP conduit programs) and sets out the transaction eligibility requirements and the conduit eligibility requirements.
paragraphs: Paragraphs (1) and (2) of the preceding Article apply mutatis mutandis to the calculation of the risk weight of a qualifying short-term STC securitization exposure.

The term "qualifying short-term STC securitization exposure" in the preceding paragraph means a securitization exposure that satisfies the requirements prescribed in the relevant item below according to the classification of securitization exposures set out in the following items: (i) a loan to, or a liquidity support or credit enhancement transaction for, ABCP or a securitization special purpose entity in an ABCP program (hereinafter in this Article referred to as an "ABCP securitization special purpose entity"): the transaction eligibility requirements and the eligibility requirements of the ABCP securitization special purpose entity; (ii) a liquidity support or credit enhancement transaction for a transaction between an ABCP securitization special purpose entity and a seller (meaning a person that sells to the ABCP securitization special purpose entity the receivables that underlie the ABCP; hereinafter the same in this Article): the transaction eligibility requirements.

The term "transaction eligibility requirements" in the items of the preceding paragraph means satisfying all of the following requirements: (i) the receivables sold by the seller satisfy all of the following: (a) where the seller sells multiple receivables, the characteristics of those receivables are homogeneous; (b) they are not securitization exposures; provided, however, that this does not apply where they are senior securitization exposures (excluding those arising from discounts not requiring refund); (ii) at the time the seller sells the receivables to the ABCP securitization special purpose entity, the sponsor (meaning a person that establishes and manages the ABCP program; hereinafter the same in this Article) can obtain information on loss experience (including delinquency status) for assets whose risk characteristics are substantially similar to those of the receivables, covering a period sufficient to grasp the risk characteristics of the receivables; (iii) at the time the seller sells the receivables to the ABCP securitization special purpose entity, the sponsor can obtain all of the following information: (a) that the receivable is not delinquent or in default and does not show signs thereof; (b) that the receivable is not one for which the seller is aware of grounds indicating a high probability of default, and is not subject to attachment, provisional attachment or other compulsory execution proceedings; (iv) confirmation by the seller or the sponsor is, in principle, conducted on the following matters: (a) that none of the receivables constituting the underlying assets of the ABCP falls under any of (1) through (4) below: (1) the obligor of the receivable has, during the three years preceding the origination of the ABCP, been subject to a decision to commence bankruptcy proceedings, a decision to commence rehabilitation proceedings, a decision to commence reorganization proceedings, an order to commence special liquidation, or a decision to recognize foreign insolvency proceedings (including foreign proceedings equivalent to these), or a specified conciliation prescribed in Article 2, paragraph (3) of the Act on Specified Conciliation for Promoting the Adjustment of Specified Debts, etc. has been concluded with respect to that obligor; (2) incident information concerning the obligor of the receivable (meaning information from which a decline in the obligor's ability to pay can be inferred, such as delinquency, debt restructuring or subrogated payment) is registered with a public credit information agency; (3) where the obligor of the receivable has been assigned a rating by an eligible credit rating agency or a similar external credit assessment, the obligor is assessed as having significantly high credit risk or as being in default; (4) a civil dispute has arisen between the original creditor of the receivable (including the originator) and the obligor; (b) that, at the time the receivables constituting the underlying assets of the ABCP are sold to the ABCP securitization special purpose entity, there has, in principle, been at least one repayment record for all of those receivables; (v) where the original creditor of the receivables sold to the ABCP securitization special purpose entity is the seller, those receivables have been originated on the basis of the seller's consistent underwriting standards, without significant deterioration in creditworthiness and without significantly deteriorating the assets. In addition, where there has been a material change in those underwriting standards, the timing and purpose of the change are disclosed by the seller to the sponsor; (vi) the receivables constituting the underlying assets of the ABCP have not been arbitrarily selected and sold by the seller; (vii) the sponsor has confirmed all of the following matters by an appropriate opinion of attorneys, etc.: (a) that the original creditor of the receivables sold to the ABCP securitization special purpose entity, the seller and other related parties do not have effective control over those receivables; (b) that the receivables are legally isolated from the original creditor, the seller and other related parties so that those parties cannot exercise control over the receivables even in their insolvency proceedings, etc.; (viii) the sponsor receives from the seller, at all of the following points in time, loan-level data on the underlying assets of the ABCP (or, where the underlying assets are highly diversified, loan-level data or stratified data from which their risk characteristics can be grasped): (a) before the seller sells the receivables to the ABCP securitization special purpose entity; (b) after the seller has sold the receivables to the ABCP securitization special purpose entity, when the sponsor so requests; (ix) redemption of the ABCP depends on the ability or willingness to repay of the obligors of the receivables that are its underlying assets; (x) where interest rate risk or foreign exchange risk exists with respect to the payment of principal and interest on the receivables sold by the seller to the ABCP securitization special purpose entity, the sponsor has confirmed that those risks are appropriately hedged; (xi) before and after the seller sells the receivables to the ABCP securitization special purpose entity, the sponsor satisfies all of the following requirements: (a) it has confirmed that the priority of payments of principal and interest on those receivables is appropriately provided for in the related contracts; (b) it can obtain information on the payment of principal and interest on those receivables (including information on matters that may affect payments); (xii) the related contracts between the sponsor and the seller clearly provide for the rights of the ABCP securitization special purpose entity where a credit event occurs with respect to the obligors of the receivables transferred to the ABCP securitization special purpose entity or with respect to the seller; (xiii) the sponsor has confirmed that the seller and other transaction parties have the ability to perform their business appropriately with a high level of expertise, and sufficient experience; (xiv) the seller has disclosed to the sponsor documents stating the following: (a) the contractual obligations and responsibilities under the contracts relating to transactions between the seller and related parties (including servicers (in (b), meaning persons entrusted, by commission or sub-commission, with the administration of the receivables sold by the seller to the ABCP securitization special purpose entity, the demand for payment of those receivables from their obligors, and the receipt of collections)); (b) matters concerning the replacement of material related parties (including servicers and persons providing liquidity support for the receivables sold by the seller to the ABCP securitization special purpose entity) upon deterioration of their creditworthiness; (xv) for all of the receivables sold by the seller to the ABCP securitization special purpose entity, the sponsor can obtain all of the following information: (a) the payment record of principal and interest on those receivables (including scheduled payment amounts, prepaid principal amounts and accrued interest amounts); (b) the delinquency status, etc. of those receivables; (c) information on income and payments other than that set out in (a) and (b); (xvi) as of the acquisition date of the receivables, the receivables are not commercial real estate-related exposures, and the risk weight of the receivables calculated pursuant to Chapter 3 (where the effects of credit risk mitigation techniques can be taken into account, the risk weight after taking those effects into account) satisfies the requirement prescribed in (a) through (c) below according to the type of receivable set out therein: (a) exposures to owner-occupied residential real estate, etc. or exposures to rental residential real estate: the risk weight obtained by taking the weighted average of the risk weights of the individual underlying assets of the ABCP (including those receivables) by their amounts in the portfolio of those underlying assets is 40% or less; (b) exposures to SMEs, etc. or retail exposures (excluding those falling under (a)): the risk weight of each individual receivable is 75% or less; (c) exposures other than those set out in (a) and (b): the risk weight of each individual receivable is 100% or less.

The term "eligibility requirements of the ABCP securitization special purpose entity" in item (i) of paragraph (2) means satisfying all of the following requirements: (i) the sponsor has substantiated and guaranteed to investors the satisfaction of the requirements set out in item (i) of the preceding paragraph, and can explain the status of that satisfaction in a timely manner; (ii) the sponsor discloses to investors information on loss experience (including delinquency status) for assets whose risk characteristics are substantially similar to those of the underlying assets, covering a period sufficient to grasp the risk characteristics of the ABCP program; (iii) the sponsor has the following number of years of experience as the sponsor of an ABCP program whose underlying assets have risk characteristics substantially similar to those of the receivables underlying the ABCP, according to the classification of receivables in (a) or (b): (a) receivables against individuals or the like: three years or more; (b) receivables other than those set out in (a): five years or more; (iv) the sponsor has substantiated and guaranteed to investors the satisfaction of the requirements set out in items (iii) and (iv) of the preceding paragraph; (v) the sponsor has substantiated and guaranteed to investors all of the following matters: (a) that it has taken measures to confirm that all underwriting policies for the receivables purchased by the ABCP securitization special purpose entity are consistent; (b) that it can explain the content of the measures in (a); (c) that, where there has been a change in the underwriting policies in (a), the sponsor can obtain the content and purpose of the change from the seller without delay; (vi) the sponsor discloses to investors its criteria for selecting sellers; (vii) the sponsor satisfies all of the following requirements: (a) it has substantiated and guaranteed to investors the result of its confirmation of the enforceability of the receivables constituting the underlying assets of the ABCP; (b) it has disclosed to investors that it has received from the seller a substantiation and guarantee that all of the receivables constituting the underlying assets of the ABCP are isolated from the seller; (viii) before the ABCP securitization special purpose entity issues the ABCP and during the term of the transaction after issuance, the sponsor provides investors with aggregate data from which the risk characteristics of the underlying assets of the ABCP can be grasped; (ix) the sponsor provides liquidity support, credit enhancement or other support against risk that pays in full, unconditionally and in a timely manner, all of the ABCP issued by the ABCP securitization special purpose entity; (x) the sponsor provides investors with the content of the liquidity support, credit enhancement or other support against risk set out in the preceding item; (xi) where interest rate risk or foreign exchange risk exists with respect to the payment of principal and interest, the sponsor has confirmed that those risks are appropriately hedged and has disclosed that fact to investors; (xii) the transaction documents between the ABCP securitization special purpose entity and investors do not contain a special provision allowing the ABCP securitization special purpose entity to extend the redemption date of the ABCP; (xiii) the sponsor satisfies all of the following requirements: (a) it has disclosed to investors that the priority of payments of principal and interest (including payments by means of credit enhancement provided to the ABCP program) is appropriately provided for in the related contracts; (b) it has substantiated and guaranteed to investors that it satisfies the requirements set out in items (xi)(a) and (b) of the preceding paragraph; (xiv) the sponsor has clearly provided, in the related contracts with investors, for the rights that investors hold when a credit event occurs with respect to the sponsor; (xv) the sponsor satisfies all of the following requirements: (a) before the ABCP securitization special purpose entity issues the ABCP, the sponsor discloses to investors, to the extent practicable, an appropriate prospectus (limited to one relating to that ABCP) that has been confirmed by attorneys, etc. (excluding in-house counsel of the sponsor itself); (b) before the seller sells receivables to the ABCP securitization special purpose entity, the sponsor can obtain, to the extent practicable, an appropriate prospectus (limited to one relating to the sale of those receivables) that has been confirmed by attorneys, etc. (excluding in-house counsel of the sponsor itself); (xvi) the seller or the sponsor bears part of the credit risk in the ABCP program in an appropriate manner. In addition, the sponsor discloses to investors the manner in which that risk is borne; (xvii) the longer of the following periods is three years or less: (a) the period calculated by taking the weighted average, by the balances of the individual underlying assets of the ABCP held by the ABCP securitization special purpose entity, of the residual maturities of those underlying assets; (b) with respect to the period set out in (a) (where that period cannot be calculated, the longest of the residual maturities of the individual underlying assets of the ABCP held by the ABCP securitization special purpose entity may be used), the period calculated by taking the weighted average by the balance of all the ABCP issued by that ABCP securitization special purpose entity; (xviii) the sponsor is a capital adequacy ratio-regulated financial institution; (xix) the sponsor can substantiate and guarantee to investors whether it satisfies all of the requirements set out in the preceding items (where information from the seller is necessary, to the extent substantiated by that seller, the sponsor can substantiate and guarantee it to investors); (xx) the sponsor satisfies all of the following requirements: (a) it has the ability to perform business relating to liquidity support and credit enhancement appropriately with a high level of expertise, and sufficient experience; (b) the transaction documents provide that it has a duty to act in the interest of investors; (xxi) the following matters are clearly stated in the transaction documents between the ABCP securitization special purpose entity and the seller, the transaction documents between the ABCP securitization special purpose entity and investors or lenders, and other transaction documents (for the transaction documents between the ABCP securitization special purpose entity and the seller, limited to the matters in (a) and (b)): (a) the contractual obligations and responsibilities of the related parties to the ABCP program; (b) matters concerning the replacement of material related parties upon deterioration of their creditworthiness; (c) the content of the liquidity support or credit enhancement for the ABCP program; (xxii) as of the date on which the ABCP securitization special purpose entity acquires receivables from the seller, the ratio of the balance of each individual receivable to the total balance of all the underlying assets of the ABCP for which that receivable is an underlying asset is 2% or less (3% or less where all of those receivables are exposures to business corporations and the seller or the sponsor holds the tranche set out in (a) or (b) below and the total amount of that tranche is 10% or more of the amount set out in (a) or (b) (including cases where the credit risk borne by the seller or the sponsor is equivalent thereto)): (a) the most junior tranche of the ABCP: the total amount of the receivables that are the underlying assets of that ABCP; (b) the most junior tranche of the receivables: the total amount of all tranches of those receivables.
